title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 185
paragraphs: As far as these Atlanteans I can give in order the names of those settled in the belt of sand, but for parts beyond this I cannot. The belt, however, extends as far as the Pillars of Heracles and also beyond them; and in it there is a mine of salt at ten days' journey from the Atlanteans, with people living there—and all of them have their houses built of lumps of salt, since these parts of Libya that we have now reached have no rain, for if it rained, the walls being made of salt could not last. The salt dug there is both white and purple in color. Above the belt of sand, in the parts toward the south wind and the interior of Libya, the country is uninhabited, without water and without wild beasts, rainless and treeless, and there is no trace of moisture in it.
